title: Whose Language Counts as High Quality? Measuring Language Ideologies in Text Data Selection
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark does not measure aspects of faith or religion. Its focus is on measuring how a text 'quality filter' prefers language associated with certain demographic and socioeconomic factors (wealth, education, urban vs. rural, school size).
findings: The paper does not present any findings related to religion from its own analysis. It only mentions in a footnote that English Wikipedia, a common training data source, is dominated by an Anglo-American perspective, citing that two of the ten most frequently mentioned people are 'prominent figures in Christianity'. This is used as background evidence for existing biases in training corpora, not as a result of the paper's primary investigation.
